exposure: Mode of birth (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
outcome: Postpartum cervical cytology results (regression, progression, stability)
cohort: The study included 59 pregnant women diagnosed with squamous intraepithelial lesions (SIL) and/or positive human papilloma virus (HPV) results.
finding: A significant reduction in abnormal cervical cytology was observed postpartum, with 30.43% of patients showing regression of lesions.
mod_finding: Higher rates of cervical lesion regression were observed after vaginal birth compared to cesarean section, although this difference was not statistically significant.
